subject: biology
title: Uses of monoclonal antibodies
key_idea: Monoclonal antibodies bind only to their specific antigen. This lets them detect a hormone in a pregnancy test, locate or identify pathogens and cancer cells, and carry a drug or toxin to cancer cells.

blocks.text: A monoclonal antibody has a shape that is complementary to one antigen only. It binds to that antigen and to nothing else.

items: A different antigen has a different shape, so the antibody does not bind to it.
A coloured bead, a fluorescent dye, a drug, a toxin or a radioactive substance can be attached to the antibody.
The attached substance is then carried to the antigen and stays there.
Monoclonal antibodies are specific. They bind only to their complementary antigen.
Something can be attached to the antibody to be carried to the target.

blocks.text: Monoclonal antibodies can be used to detect a molecule or pathogen. The test shows a colour or a dye when the antigen is present.

items: The test detects a hormone (hCG) in urine.
The hormone binds to antibodies on the test, which have a coloured bead attached.
Immobile (fixed) antibodies in the test window hold the bound hormone, so a coloured line appears.
To see pathogens, a fluorescent dye is bound to the antibodies. They are put on a slide of the sample and rinsed.
The antibodies bind to the pathogens, which show up under the microscope.
Antibodies can be used to locate cancer cells or blood clots, or to detect the A antigen on red blood cells to identify a blood group.
Antibodies can also be used to identify pathogens, develop vaccines and test drugs.
A pregnancy test uses antibodies that bind to a hormone in urine and show a coloured line.
A fluorescent dye on the antibody shows where pathogens or target cells are.

blocks.text: Monoclonal antibodies can deliver treatment straight to the cells that need it.

diagram.alt: Sort each description into the use of monoclonal antibodies it belongs to: pregnancy testing, diagnosis, or treatment.
diagram.prompt: Which use does each description belong to?

items.text: Binds to a hormone in urine
A coloured bead makes a line appear
A fluorescent dye shows pathogens on a slide
Locates cancer cells in the body
Carries a toxin, drug or radioactive substance to cancer cells
Binds to a donor organ's cells so white blood cells cannot attack them

items: To treat cancer, the antibody is attached to a radioactive substance, a toxin or a drug.
The antibody only attaches to antigens on cancer cells, so the substance stops them growing or dividing, or kills them.
Some antibodies instead interrupt the cell cycle or help the immune system to kill the cancer cells.
After a transplant, an antibody can bind to antigens on the donor cells. White blood cells' antibodies then cannot bind to them.
Monoclonal antibodies are not used as widely as first hoped, because they cause more side effects than expected.
In treatment, the antibody carries a drug, toxin or radioactive substance to the target cells.
It only binds to its target, so healthy cells are less affected.

checks.q: Explain why a monoclonal antibody for a hormone does not bind to other molecules in urine.
checks.a: The antibody is complementary in shape to the hormone only. Other molecules have a different shape.

checks.q: Describe how monoclonal antibodies can be used to treat cancer.
checks.a: The antibody is attached to a radioactive substance, toxin or drug. It binds only to antigens on cancer cells, so the substance stops the cancer cells growing or kills them.

checks.q: Give two uses of monoclonal antibodies.
checks.a: Any two from: pregnancy testing, detecting diseases or cancer, treating disease or cancer.

exam_phrases: mAbs will bind to pathogens and show up under the microscope
monoclonal antibody is attached to radioactive substance / toxin / drug / chemical
monoclonal antibody will (only) attach to / target (antigen on) cancer cells
monoclonal antibodies are complementary (in shape) to (liver) antigen

mistakes.wrong: Add the monoclonal antibodies and the dye to the slide.
mistakes.right: Adding them unbound is ignored. The dye is bound to the antibody first, then the fluorescent antibodies are put on the slide.

mistakes.wrong: The monoclonal antibody is the same shape as the antigen.
mistakes.right: This is not accepted. The antibody is complementary in shape to the antigen.

mistakes.wrong: The antibodies released by phagocytes cannot bind to the donor cells.
mistakes.right: Phagocytes do not release antibodies. Say antibodies released by white blood cells (lymphocytes) cannot bind to the cells.

worked_example.question:
A monoclonal antibody has been produced to treat pancreatic cancer.

Explain how the monoclonal antibody works to treat pancreatic cancer.
answer_points: The monoclonal antibody is attached to a radioactive substance, toxin, drug or chemical.
The monoclonal antibody will only attach to (target) antigens on cancer cells or the tumour.
So the radioactive substance, toxin, drug or chemical stops the cancer cells growing or dividing, or kills them.
worked_example.tip: A second route also scores: the antibody interrupts the cell cycle or aids the immune response, only targets cancer cells, and so stops them growing or helps the immune system destroy them.

exam_phrases: (pregnancy test detects) a hormone in urine
(hormone / antigen) binds to the antibody (on the test)
which have a coloured (bead) attached to them
there are immobile antibodies (in the test window)
the shape of the antibody is complementary to the A antigen
it will not bind to the B antigen

mistakes.right: Say what is detected: a hormone (hCG) in urine, which binds to antibodies that have a coloured bead attached.

mistakes.wrong: The antibody does not react with blood group B because it does not match.
mistakes.right: Explain: the shape of the antibody is complementary to the A antigen, the B antigen has a different shape, so the antibody will not bind to it.

worked_example.question:
Monoclonal antibodies can be used in the diagnosis of genetic disorders and pregnancy testing.

Describe how a pregnancy test uses monoclonal antibodies to show that a woman is pregnant.
answer_points: The pregnancy test detects a hormone (hCG) in urine.
The hormone binds to the antibody on the test.
These antibodies have a coloured bead attached to them.
A line appears because there are immobile antibodies in the test window.
worked_example.tip: Any four points score one mark each. Accepted: the antibodies move up the strip and colour appears.

mistakes.wrong: Monoclonal antibodies are used in medicine.
mistakes.right: Be specific. Name a use: pregnancy testing, detecting diseases or cancer, or treating disease or cancer.

mistakes.wrong: They treat cancer by killing all the cells in the body.
mistakes.right: The antibody is specific. It carries the substance to the cancer cells only.

worked_example.question:
Large quantities of one type of antibody can be made. These antibodies are called monoclonal antibodies.

Give two uses of monoclonal antibodies.
worked_example.tip: Any two of these score one mark each. Specific diseases, pathogen identification, vaccine development and drug testing are also allowed.
